correctness.rationale: For T with half-bases A>B>0 and height H>0, symmetry reduces random line direction to theta uniform in [0,pi/2]. Its support width equals 2A cos(theta) until alpha=atan((A-B)/H), then (A+B)cos(theta)+H sin(theta)=Q*cos(theta-beta), Q=sqrt((A+B)^2+H²), beta=atan(H/(A+B)); the switching height is z=2AH/sqrt((A-B)^2+H²). Branchwise change of variables yields the stated exact 2/pi times inverse-root density. Monotonic second branch (beta<alpha), stationary switching (beta=alpha), and interior second-branch maximum (beta>alpha) produce pole coefficients 2/pi at 2A and respectively none, 2/pi or 4/pi at Q; when Q=2A the coefficients add to 6/pi. These cases identify A and the angular regime. The support minimum is min(H,z); where this is H, recover B from the perimeter mean P=pi*E[W]/2=A+B+sqrt((A-B)²+H²) or from Q²=(A+B)²+H². In z<H cases, subtract the now-known first and increasing second branches to identify the H onset of the remaining density, then recover B. Rectangles (A=B) have a single 4/pi pole at Q and support min=min(2A,H), recovering their two side lengths as an unordered pair. This exhausts the transition and pole-merger boundaries; exact-law injectivity holds only within the isosceles trapezoid class.
